AnalysisCoverageSection.description:
Snapshot rollup of per-service analysis coverage (§5.4.3).

Rollup sums cover only services whose counts are known; the per-service
listing is where unknowns stay visible. Low coverage is a *finding*
(dead code and/or unreached roots — T4's scope), not an error.

coverage_percent.description: None when no service has known counts
coverage_percent.title: Coverage Percent

production_methods.description: Sum over services with known counts
production_methods.title: Production Methods

services.description: One entry per analyzed service (libraries excluded, §5.2.6), sorted by name
services.title: Services

AnalysisCoverageSection.title: AnalysisCoverageSection

AuthCoverageSection.description:
Snapshot rollup of what the auth layer could and could not read (§5.2.9).

The standing tracking mechanism for auth blind spots, playing the role
``cfg_anomalies`` plays for control flow: an idiom wadi cannot interpret
stays counted here rather than living in prose, so the next tranche is
scheduled by measured demand rather than intuition.

composition_unresolved.description: §5.2.12: endpoints where several guards apply and how they COMBINE was not read. Their listed requirements may be alternatives, so this is the counter that stops the relationship numbers being read as exact
composition_unresolved.title: Composition Unresolved

extraction_gaps.description: §5.2.10: independent-oracle findings per AuthGapCode. Every other counter here is derived from evidence the auth layer EMITTED, so a construct dropped before emission is invisible to them — this is the one that can see a miss
extraction_gaps.title: Extraction Gaps

no_evidence.description: No claim because nothing that could gate was found
no_evidence.title: No Evidence

relationship_scoped.description: §5.2.12: endpoints whose policy is a RELATION to a resource rather than a role. Counted apart from `authenticated` because it answers a different question — a system where this dominates has a role list that is empty for a reason, not by omission
relationship_scoped.title: Relationship Scoped

request_policies.description: §5.2.10 T6: CORS/CSRF/rejection-handling declarations per kind, across all services. Counted apart from every claim counter above because they gate REACH, not principal — a system with `csrf disabled` everywhere is a fact worth reading, and it changes none of the authenticated/withheld numbers
request_policies.title: Request Policies

unexercised_vocabulary.description: Auth vocabulary this snapshot contains ZERO instances of (§5.2.11 T6). A zero counter is otherwise ambiguous: it may mean wadi looked and the system genuinely has none, or that this corpus never exercises the idiom and the zero is evidence of nothing. Naming the second case stops a reader taking `denied: 0` as proof the denial path works
unexercised_vocabulary.title: Unexercised Vocabulary

unread_by_kind.description: Enforcement points detected but not readable, counted per AuthEvidenceKind
unread_by_kind.title: Unread By Kind

withheld.description: No claim because an in-scope guard could not be read
withheld.title: Withheld

AuthCoverageSection.title: AuthCoverageSection

CfgAnomaly.description:
One structural-invariant violation family on a service's CFGs
(§5.2.8 M2, schema 1.8.0). Never an error: the weird code lives in real
repos, and a violated invariant is a queryable fact about how much the
graph can be trusted (P10).

sample_sites.description: Up to 5 example sites — examples, never the exhaustive list
sample_sites.title: Sample Sites

CfgAnomaly.title: CfgAnomaly

CfgAnomalyCode.description:
§5.2.8 M2 structural-invariant violation codes.

Evaluated against the RAW exported CFG of every method on every snapshot —
before the assembler's synthetic entry/exit patching, which would make
reachability invariants vacuously true. Additive changes bump
``SCHEMA_VERSION`` minor.

An enum rather than a string registry (§7, recorded 2026-08-05): pyright
catches producer/registry drift in CI, which a runtime validator could
only catch on a user's repository.
CfgAnomalyCode.title: CfgAnomalyCode

CfgAnomalySection.description:
Snapshot rollup of ICFG structural-invariant violations (§5.2.8 M2).

Every snapshot is a continuous CFG test: a violation is a queryable fact
about how far the graph can be trusted for that code, never an error.

services.description: One entry per analyzed service (libraries excluded), sorted by name
services.title: Services

CfgAnomalySection.title: CfgAnomalySection

CoverageTotals.description: Aggregate counts for a snapshot's stitched graph.

async_rooted_call_sites.description: Subset of unreachable_call_sites reached from a NON-HTTP root (startup runner, scheduled task, listener). These really execute — they are not stitched because no request is behind them, not because they are dead (§5.2.11 T2)
async_rooted_call_sites.title: Async Rooted Call Sites

suspected_call_sites.description: HTTP-shaped calls on receivers the CPG could not type-resolve — never matched, never blended into resolved results (P7); detail rows live in remote_calls with suspected=true
suspected_call_sites.title: Suspected Call Sites

unreachable_call_sites.description: Sink call sites outside the endpoint-reachable closure — excluded from the map by design, inventoried so the exclusion is queryable (§5.2.5; detail rows live in remote_calls with reachable=false)
unreachable_call_sites.title: Unreachable Call Sites

CoverageTotals.title: CoverageTotals

EndpointCollision.description:
Two endpoints of one service derived the SAME content-derived id
(§7, recorded 2026-08-05, schema 1.18.0).

Endpoint ids are ``hash(service, verb, simplified_uri)`` and the store
upserts on ``(snapshot_id, service_id, id)``, so a collision does not
merge — the second row *replaces* the first and the endpoint is gone. That
is how three handlers of a real controller vanished with every honesty
surface reading clean: the loss happens at the storage key, downstream of
everything that counts.

Recorded as a fact rather than resolved silently, because the alternatives
are both worse. Failing the service would cost a whole map to one duplicate
pair; picking a winner quietly is exactly the behaviour that hid the bug.
A deterministic winner is kept so the snapshot stays reproducible, and the
losers are named here with their handlers so the cause is one click away.

**Cause-independent by design.** The 2026-08-05 instance came from URI
truncation, but any future defect that makes two URIs equal — a bad
normalizer, an over-eager simplification — lands here too. Expected empty
in healthy operation; non-empty means endpoints were dropped.

dropped_handlers.description: Handler signatures whose endpoints were lost to the collision
dropped_handlers.title: Dropped Handlers

kept_handler.description: Handler signature of the endpoint that was stored
kept_handler.title: Kept Handler

uri.description: The simplified URI they collapsed onto
uri.title: Uri

EndpointCollision.title: EndpointCollision

ExternalApiEntry.description: A real dependency on an address outside the analyzed system.
ExternalApiEntry.title: ExternalApiEntry

PlaceholderEntry.description:
A config-resolved service name with no analyzed service behind it —
honest partial coverage and a 'grant access to this repo' to-do item.
PlaceholderEntry.title: PlaceholderEntry

QuarantinedFact.description:
A diagnostic fact whose vocabulary this build does not recognize
(§7, recorded 2026-08-05, schema 1.16.0).

Never fatal and never dropped. Diagnostic facts describe how well analysis
read the code, not the code itself, so an unreadable one must not cost the
map — but silently discarding it would be the exact gap the registries
exist to prevent (P10, turned on wadi's own pipeline: a self-observation we
cannot parse is itself a queryable fact).

Expected **empty in all healthy operation**, unlike ``cfg_anomalies``,
which is expected non-zero on real code forever. That difference is why it
has its own home rather than sharing one: an always-zero signal folded into
an always-noisy one stops being a signal. Non-empty on the fixtures or
benchmarks fails CI, while a user's run only ever loses the one footnote.

registry.description: Which vocabulary rejected it, e.g. 'CfgAnomalyCode' or 'async-root'
registry.title: Registry

sample_anchor.description: One example site, when the rejected fact carried one

service_id.description: Owning service; None on a snapshot-level artifact
service_id.title: Service Id

QuarantinedFact.title: QuarantinedFact

ServiceCfgAnomalyEntry.description:
§5.2.8 M2: one service's structural-invariant violations.

Services that were never checked (extraction failed, pre-1.8 snapshot)
carry ``checked=False`` with no anomalies — unknown is never conflated
with clean (P10).

anomalies.description: Per-code counts with sample sites; empty when checked and clean
anomalies.title: Anomalies

checked.description: False = invariants never ran for this service
checked.title: Checked

name.description: Service display name, denormalized for reads
name.title: Name

ServiceCfgAnomalyEntry.title: ServiceCfgAnomalyEntry

ServiceCoverageEntry.description:
Analysis coverage of one service (§5.4.3).

``None`` counts mean the fact is unavailable for this service (extraction
failed, or the snapshot predates the metric) — unknown is reported as
unknown, never as zero (P10).

coverage_percent.description: reachable/production * 100, 1dp; None when unknown or 0 methods
coverage_percent.title: Coverage Percent

name.description: Service display name, denormalized for reads
name.title: Name

ServiceCoverageEntry.title: ServiceCoverageEntry

SourceAnchor.description:
A file + line range in the text that was actually analyzed.

For preprocessed files (delombok) the anchor refers to the generated
variant — source-on-demand serves that same text, so anchors and served
source stay aligned by construction (§5.3).

file.description: Path relative to the service build root
file.title: File

SourceAnchor.title: SourceAnchor

SourceVariant.description:
Whether an anchor refers to original repo text or a generated variant (§5.3).

``GENERATED`` marks preprocessor output (e.g. delombok'ed Java) — the text
that was actually analyzed, served by source-on-demand with a badge.
SourceVariant.title: SourceVariant

UnmodelledMechanismEntry.description:
A client library the census detected but no sink pass models (§5.4.2).

The yas lesson: a system whose calls all use an unmodelled client produced
a clean-looking zero-edge coverage report. This entry is the truthful
sentence — "present, unmodelled" — never a call count (imports are not
calls, P10).

mechanism.description: KNOWN_CLIENT_LIBRARIES value outside the modelled set
mechanism.title: Mechanism

UnmodelledMechanismEntry.title: UnmodelledMechanismEntry

UnresolvedCallEntry.description:
One call site the stitcher could not resolve, with the reason stated.

``reason_code`` is machine-readable so limitations are queryable, not just
prose — e.g. counting how often Lombok-generated interiors block URL
recovery is a coverage query, not an investigation.
UnresolvedCallEntry.title: UnresolvedCallEntry

description:
What the map knows it doesn't know (§5.4) — surfaced FIRST everywhere.

Snapshot-level; the stitcher is this collection's single writer (P4).
Hint fields are reserved now so the schema is hint-ready; hints themselves
ship in Phase 4 (§11).

analysis_coverage.description: How much of the source the analysis walked (§5.4.3, schema 1.5.0). None only on reports written before the metric existed

applied_hint_ids.description: Reserved — stitching hints land in Phase 4
applied_hint_ids.title: Applied Hint Ids

auth_coverage.description: What the auth layer could and could not read (§5.2.9, schema 1.13.0). None only on reports written before the enforcement model existed

cfg_anomalies.description: ICFG structural-invariant violations (§5.2.8 M2, schema 1.8.0). None only on reports written before the invariants existed

endpoint_collisions.description: Endpoints that derived the same content-derived id and so could not all be stored (§7, schema 1.18.0), rolled up across services. **Expected empty**: non-empty means the inventory is missing endpoints the analysis actually found — the loss happens at the storage key, downstream of every other counter here
endpoint_collisions.title: Endpoint Collisions

phonebook_conflicts.description: Config identities claimed by more than one source (never silently picked)
phonebook_conflicts.title: Phonebook Conflicts

quarantined_facts.description: Diagnostic facts whose vocabulary this build does not recognize (§7, schema 1.16.0), rolled up across services. **Expected empty**: non-empty means version drift between a producer and its registry, never a property of the analyzed code. CI fails on non-empty for the fixtures and benchmarks; a user's run only loses the footnote
quarantined_facts.title: Quarantined Facts

stale_hint_ids.description: Reserved — stitching hints land in Phase 4
stale_hint_ids.title: Stale Hint Ids

unmodelled_mechanisms.description: Client libraries present but not modelled by any sink pass (§5.4.2 census) — a zero-edge system is distinguishable from a correct zero-edge answer
unmodelled_mechanisms.title: Unmodelled Mechanisms
